subject: Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value

messages.author: e1af1b5e367974aa
messages.subject: Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value
parts:
Hi all,


I've slowly been expanding a complicated hierarchical model: I evaluate the effects of three between-subject and one within-subject variables on four outcome variables. Initially, I included no interaction terms and the model ran fine, giving sensible results (as per intuition + PPC). However, as I've been adding interaction terms - the model attached includes four-way interactions (full factorial) - the model has been throwing more errors when I try to run it. Namely: "Error in function boost::math::cyl_bessel_i<double>(double,double): numeric overflow" and "Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value", and, fatally, "Initialization between (--2, -2) failed after 100 attempts". 


Does anyone have any immediate ideas as to what the problem might be and/or potential solutions to it? Or, does anyone have any suggestions about how to troubleshoot this?


I am really hoping someone can provide some insight without having to dive into the details of the model, since, understandably, it is rather elaborate at this point. 


Cheers,


Ghislain d'Entremont

Hi,

We are using the 'tan trick' here to reparameterize the Cauchy, so the SDs should have half-cauchy priors (0,1).

Cheers,

Ghislain

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value
parts:
You need to track down where your program runs into errors.
That's why we included print() statements, but there's a hitch.
I think all of our interfaces are broken in that they don't print
if the model block rejects---you only see the rejected message.
And I'm afraid this didn't get fixed in 2.10 because we never
created an issue with a 2.10 milestone. I'm going to fix that.

So you need to remove everyting in your model and build it up
a bit at a time to see where the numerics go bad.

- Bob
